newsitem.title: USA: U.S West Coast products prices steady in late talk.
newsitem.headline: U.S West Coast products prices steady in late talk.

text.p: U.S. West Coast products prices were mostly steady in late thin trade, with traders paying more attention to regional supply than declines on NYMEX.
"Gasoline's been long on the West Coast, demand is weak," one refinery trader said, noting the end of driving season put more supply into the markets.
NYMEX heating oil settled off 2.22 cents to 73.97 cents a gallon, while front-month crude dropped 47 cents to $25.07 a barrel.
Reports of higher-than-expected distillate builds prompted the NYMEX downturn.

One trader said Chevron's El Segundo, California, plant would begin a scheduled turnaround on its fluid catalytic cracker this week.
Bids for Los Angeles conventional regular grade gasoline continued steady all day at 63/64 cents a gallon, with San Francisco grades a notional 1.50 cents cheaper.
Refinery buying slowed as profits were squeezed by low retail gasoline prices and relatively expensive crude futures prices, traders said.
Offers for CARB-grade gasoline added another half cent to their earlier penny drop, hitting 69.50 cents a gallon late. Bids for CARB gasoline fell half a cent to 68.50 cents.
Los Angeles low-sulphur diesel also stayed at 70.25/71 cents.
But CARB diesel, buoyed by strengthening demand and refiners' slow switchover from jet fuel production, saw prices higher at 85.50 cents.
"There's been a huge demand from planting in the central (California) valley," one trader said, referring to wintertime planting in the state. "That's the strongest product by far."
